How appointments are booked, changed and cancelled, and what happens when one is missed.

Source: Appointments & Cancellations (as of 2026-02-01)

If you arrive more than fifteen minutes late, we may not be able to complete the planned treatment, because the appointment after yours belongs to someone else. We will do what fits in the remaining time and book a second visit for the rest, at no extra charge for splitting it.

Source: Appointments & Cancellations > Late Arrivals (as of 2026-02-01)

Ask to be added to the waitlist when you book. If an earlier slot opens up, we call people on the waitlist in order.

Source: Appointments & Cancellations > Same-Day Openings and the Waitlist (as of 2026-02-01)

Arrive ten minutes before the appointment time. A first visit usually includes a full examination, X-rays if they are needed, and a conversation about a treatment plan.

Source: New Patients > Arriving for Your First Appointment (as of 2026-01-15)

We see children. A parent or legal guardian must attend the first visit and sign the consent form; after that, an adult who is not the guardian may bring the child if we have written permission on file.

Source: New Patients > Bringing a Child (as of 2026-01-15)

The first twenty-four hours matter most. Bite gently on the gauze for about thirty minutes.

Source: Aftercare > After an Extraction (as of 2026-03-01)

A severe, throbbing ache that starts two to four days after an extraction, often spreading to the ear, can mean the clot has been lost. This is uncomfortable but easily treated: we clean and dress the socket and the pain usually settles quickly.

Source: Aftercare > After an Extraction > Dry Socket (as of 2026-03-01)

A temporary crown is held with soft cement so it can be removed later. Avoid sticky sweets and chewing gum on that side, and floss by pulling the floss out sideways rather than up, so you do not lift the temporary off.

Source: Aftercare > After a Crown (as of 2026-03-01)

This is the one true dental emergency where minutes matter. Pick the tooth up by the crown, never the root.

Source: Dental Emergencies > A Knocked-Out Adult Tooth (as of 2026-02-15)

There is metered street parking on the avenue, which is easiest in the middle of the day and difficult at school drop-off and pick-up times. A paid parking garage sits one block north.

Source: Visiting the Clinic > Parking (as of 2026-01-15)

Who can see your dental records, how to get a copy, and how we treat your information.

Source: Records & Privacy (as of 2026-01-15)

How billing works at this practice. Whether a particular plan is accepted, and what a specific treatment costs, are questions for the front desk or the assistant, which check them against our current records rather than a document like this one.

Source: Insurance & Payment (as of 2026-01-15)

A filling repairs a tooth damaged by decay. The decayed part is removed, the space is cleaned and then filled with a tooth-coloured composite material that is hardened with a light.

Source: Procedures Explained > Fillings (as of 2026-03-01)

A crown is a cap that covers a whole tooth, used when too much of the tooth is missing or cracked for a filling to hold. It normally takes two visits.

Source: Procedures Explained > Crowns (as of 2026-03-01)

A root canal treats infection inside a tooth. The inflamed tissue is removed, the canals are cleaned and sealed, and the tooth is then usually restored with a crown, because a treated tooth is more brittle.

Source: Procedures Explained > Root Canals (as of 2026-03-01)

Rinse with warm salt water and floss gently around the tooth to remove anything trapped. Over-the-counter pain relief that you have taken safely before is reasonable in the meantime.

Source: Dental Emergencies > Toothache (as of 2026-02-15)

Gums may be tender and teeth sensitive to cold for several days. Rinse with warm salt water, and use a soft brush gently along the gum line rather than avoiding the area, which slows healing.

Source: Aftercare > After a Deep Cleaning (as of 2026-03-01)

A small number of patients are advised to take an antibiotic an hour before certain dental treatment, usually because of a specific heart condition or a joint replacement. If you have been told this applies to you, say so when you book, not on the day: the prescription has to be in hand before the appointment.

Source: Before Your Visit > Antibiotics Before Treatment (as of 2026-02-15)

The entrance is step-free and the door is wide enough for a wheelchair. The treatment rooms and the toilet are on one level, with no internal steps.

Source: Visiting the Clinic > Accessibility (as of 2026-01-15)
